editorial:
You meet Nick and Suzanne as they try to give their blended family a fresh start in the suburbs. Their new house looks like a dream at first, but it quickly turns into a messy renovation nightmare. A contractor with strange methods keeps changing the plan, and every fix seems to create a bigger problem. The movie leans on loud family chaos, slapstick home disasters, and the stress of moving, so you get a light, silly tone rather than a deep story.

The cast keeps things energetic, especially the contractor scenes, but the jokes can feel repetitive and the plot is pretty predictable. If you want a cozy family movie night with kids, it works as background entertainment, though adults may find the humor thin. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray if you want a physical copy.
endingExplained: In the final stretch, Nick finally confronts Chuck after the renovation spirals out of control and the house seems beyond saving. Instead of a simple villain reveal, Chuck shows he has been pushing the project because he cares about the family and the town. The house gets finished, Nick and Suzanne stop fighting the process, and they settle into suburban life with the kids. The last beat lands on family togetherness rather than a perfect home.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves family comedies and home renovation chaos.
